subject.title: config: use datetime suffix for config backup files instead of numeric rotation

question: Should the datetime-suffix migration preserve or convert existing numbered `.bak.N` recovery files before merge, or may the new cleanup intentionally prune them?
rationale: Config backups can be a user's only rollback path, and the repository treats config migration and fallback behavior as compatibility-sensitive, so automation should not decide to delete released backup files without maintainer intent.

options.title: Preserve Legacy Recovery Points
options.body: Require this PR or a replacement to keep existing `.bak.1` through `.bak.4` files until converted or until the datetime retention set is safely populated.

options.title: Accept Timestamp-Only Pruning
options.body: Allow the first cleanup after upgrade to delete numbered backups in exchange for a strict datetime-only backup set.

options.title: Keep The Numbered Ring
options.body: Decline the suffix migration for now and keep the documented five-slot numbered recovery model.

recommendation.title: Preserve Legacy Recovery Points
recommendation.body: Require this PR or a replacement to keep existing `.bak.1` through `.bak.4` files until converted or until the datetime retention set is safely populated.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the clearest history on the backup helper and adjacent config-backup test behavior, plus the strongest routing signal for a config compatibility decision.
